text:
mira: Heads-up — noticed a steady GPU memory climb on long-context cont-batching runs. Looks like KV fragmentation + a compaction/eviction oscillation. p95 latency spikes while memory grows.

sam: Can you paste the repro and a small log? Is this on dedicated or host? :thinking:

mira: Dedicated cluster (g3-resv). Repro is a 10k-token stream across many concurrent short+long sessions (mix 70/30). Command I used:
```
./run_perf.sh --model=open-llama-65b --seq=10240 --concurrent=220 --batching=continuous --merge-timeout-ms=8
```
Logs (trimmed):
```
[kvcache] eviction_rate=12/s frag_ratio=0.42 free_slots=1200 used_slots=3400
[batch] merge_ops=4300 split_ops=4100 hol_wait_ms=72
[perf] p95=120ms p99=320ms mem_gpu=14.3GB -> 17.8GB (over 30m)
```

jon: Hmm those merge/split counts are suspiciously balanced — thrashing. If merges pick batches that touch high-residency contexts you get head-of-line blocking while eviction/compaction runs. We saw something similar in 1748004321 but this looks different (oscillation between compaction and eviction rather than a single leak).

linda: Could be alignment: small fragments between large KV ranges prevent reuse, then compaction frees some, then new batches reallocate causing fragmentation again. Any flamegraphs/alloc traces?

mira: Uploaded a flamegraph to the perf bucket: https://perf.redwood/internal/fg/2954321000-kv-oscill.svg
Top stacks show a spike in `kv_reclaim()` called from `batch_merge_worker()` and long waits on `kv_slot_lock`.

perf-bot: CI perf run 2954321000-run: regressions flagged: p95 +34%, GPU mem +2.5GB at 30m mark, eviction count increased x2. See https://ci.redwood/inference/2954321000

sam: Quick hypothesis: merge timeout of 8ms is too aggressive for mixed long-context traffic. We merge small short sessions with long ones, creating heterogeneous batches that touch many different KV ranges -> lots of KV slot churn.

mira: I ran a small A/B: increase merge-timeout to 40ms and also try `prefer_coalesce=true` in kv allocator. Results (30m window):
```
merge-timeout=8ms: p95=120ms mem-rise=3.5GB evict/s=12
merge-timeout=40ms: p95=86ms mem-rise=0.9GB evict/s=4
prefer_coalesce=true: further reduces frag_ratio 0.42 -> 0.21
```
So increasing timeout reduced HOL blocking and gave allocator time to coalesce.

jon: Interesting. But 40ms might increase tail latency for tiny bursty workloads. We need a heuristic: if batch composition includes >X% long-context tokens, increase merge timeout dynamically.

linda: Alternative approach: add a lightweight compaction pass that runs when GPU utilization < threshold. Coalesce adjacent free slots without full eviction. That could reduce oscillation without hurting p99.

mira: Also saw that when context >64k tokens the KV index entries spike and our slot allocation starts using many small fragments. Maybe we should special-case long contexts to pin contiguous slot ranges or reserve a sliding window to avoid fragmentation.

sam: Idea: batch-merge ordering should be sequence-aware: prefer merging batches whose KV ranges are contiguous or non-overlapping. That'll reduce slot reuse churn.

perf-bot: Experiment matrix queued: change A) merge-timeout 8/20/40ms, B) prefer_coalesce toggle, C) merge-order heuristic on/off. Benchmarks scheduled across 3 shards.

mira: I'll file an issue with logs, flamegraph, and the small AB results and assign it to eng-runtime. Meantime I'll push a canary that sets merge-timeout=40ms for low-util dedicated pools.

jon: For the issue, please include the minimal repro, numbers, and a proposed metric to track: frag_ratio, evict/s, batch_hol_wait_ms, p95. Also link to the flamegraph.

linda: Agreed. I'll prototype the coalesce pass. If it reduces frag_ratio by >=30% in perf runs, we consider landing as opt-in.

mira: Thanks everyone. Action items:
- mira: open issue + canary (merge-timeout=40ms) — due EOD
- linda: prototype compaction coalesce patch — check-in by Fri
- sam: add dynamic heuristic doc + test plan
- jon: add instrumentation for contiguous-KV-aware merge ordering

sam: @mira please ping once canary is live so SRE can monitor regressions. :thumbsup:

mira: Will do. Recording thread for follow-ups.
